title: The Louvain doctors before Jansenius
source_text: XXIII. Caeterum sub finem saeculi superioris, & pluribus annis antequam Jansenius scriberet, Doctores Lovanienses nullam quoque gratiam ad conversionem hominis sufficientem agnoverunt, praeter eam quae illum reapse & actu convertit. Affirmant enim subsidium quod aliquando administratur iis, qui neque credunt, neque convertuntur ad Dominum, non esse sufficiens ad fidem & conversionem, quoniam gratia ad conversionem sufficiens ipsa convertit; quae vero non convertit, non sufficit. In Justificatione censurae adversus Jesuitas Lovanienses capite 16.
pass_a_gloss: XXIII. Moreover toward the end of the previous century, and many years before Jansenius wrote, the Louvain Doctors also acknowledged no grace sufficient for the conversion of man, besides that which really and actually converts him. For they affirm that the aid which is sometimes administered to those, who neither believe, nor are converted to the Lord, is not sufficient for faith and conversion, since grace sufficient for conversion itself converts; but that which does not convert, does not suffice. In the Justification of the censure against the Jesuits of Louvain chapter 16.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXIII. Moreover, toward the end of the last century and many years before Jansenius wrote, the doctors of Louvain likewise recognized no grace sufficient for a person's conversion except the grace that actually converts him.

They maintain that the help sometimes given to those who neither believe nor turn to the Lord is not sufficient for faith and conversion, because grace sufficient for conversion converts of itself, and grace that does not convert does not suffice. Justificatio of the censure against the Louvain Jesuits, chapter 16.
